record.excerpt: Rule 2: Don't Buy Until There's a Dip Greater Than 5% from the Most Recent High Price … The DCA case assumed our investor spent $1 on Bitcoin every day from May 1, 2013 until May 23, 2021 … $1/Day – >5% Dips (Rule 2) | $2943 | 4.639 … $1/Day – >10% Dips (Rule 3) | $2943 | 4.42 … the data is clear: dollar cost averaging works better than buying the dip.
record.performance_claim: dollar cost averaging works better than buying the dip
record.notes: Accumulation rule (save $1/day, deploy on >5%/>10% dip from recent high) vs daily DCA; a negative claim, nice contrast. Bold markers removed from table cells.

spec.claim_summary: Buying only on days more than 5% below the recent high accumulates less bitcoin than buying $1 every day.
spec.untestable_reason: The claim compares repeated overlapping $1 daily versus dip-only accumulation by total BTC accumulated, which requires a DCA ladder with differing capital that the single-position engine cannot replicate.
assumptions: Asset BTCUSDT chosen for Bitcoin named in claim.
Timeframe 1d assumed; claim states daily purchases but no bar timeframe.
Direction long because rule describes buying.
'Most Recent High Price' lookback is vague; 365 bars used as placeholder only.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: repeated $1-per-day accumulation versus $1-only-on-dip-days accumulation, overlapping positions, differing total dollars deployed, and comparison by total BTC accumulated cannot be expressed in single-position one-at-a-time engine.

evidence.quote: Don't Buy Until There's a Dip
Dip Greater Than 5% from the Most Recent High Price

issues.problem: Claim is repeated accumulation: $1 on Bitcoin every day vs $1 only on >5% dip days, judged by total BTC accumulated. Spec compiles this to a single one-at-a-time long entry held via max_hold_bars, omitting repeated overlapping buys and differing total dollars deployed. Single-trade timing is not the claimed DCA accumulation comparison and could flip the verdict. Marking it NOT EXPRESSIBLE in assumptions does not fix the change in what is tested.

report.headline: This claim can't be turned into rules anyone could check.
reasons: The claim compares repeated overlapping $1 daily versus dip-only accumulation by total BTC accumulated, which requires a DCA ladder with differing capital that the single-position engine cannot replicate.
